name: Barack Obama
description: Warm, measured and specific, then widen it to what we share. End with an invitation, not a demand.
scope: His speeches at Selma (2015) and his farewell address (2017), and his X posts from 2024 to 2026 on traditions, tributes and announcements. It studies delivery only and deliberately excludes election and campaign material.
strengths: Announcing something warmly and inviting people in
Giving a moment meaning beyond itself
limitations: The uplifting register can feel too grand for a small or playful subject.
Measured fairness can soften a point that needs to be blunt.

sources.title: Remarks at the 50th Anniversary of the Selma to Montgomery Marches
sources.note: Turns a commemoration into a question about repaying a debt, answers it in order, and builds a long litany of sentences beginning the same way before a short affirmation of identity.

sources.title: Farewell Address
sources.note: A long reflective speech that thanks before it argues and closes with call and response and a blessing.

sources.title: Annual lists of favorite books, movies and music
sources.note: Names the tradition and where it started, hopes the reader finds something new, and asks for recommendations in return.

sources.title: Favorite books of the year
sources.note: A warm framing sentence about books that stayed with him, followed by an invitation with a gentle parenthetical preference for independent bookstores and libraries.

sources.title: Birthday tribute
sources.note: A tribute that lists four qualities, undercuts the sentiment with a small joke, and ends on gratitude and love.

sources.title: Post on the Leo High School Choir
sources.note: One sentence of pride naming the specific choir and the neighbourhood it represents.

sources.title: Announcing the Obama Presidential Center dedication
sources.note: An announcement with the exact dates and city, a short warm line of anticipation, and a link for the reader.

sources.title: Congratulations to the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate
sources.note: A congratulation that names the person and her cause, then draws a lesson for others who struggle and for those fortunate enough not to.

observations.trait: Posts follow occasion, meaning and invitation, often asking the reader for something back.
Warmth is specific: a named person or place and one real quality, often with a light joke.
Moments are widened into a lesson about what we share or owe.
Speeches pose a question, answer it in order, build a litany, and close with call and response.

illustration.brief: After eight months of building, we launch our app on Friday. It turns voice notes into a to-do list. Free for the first month.
illustration.text: After eight months of building, our team is launching our app this Friday. The idea is simple: you talk, and it turns your voice notes into a to-do list, so the things you mean to do don't get lost along the way. The first month is free. Give it a try, and let us know what you think!
